reasoning_traces.think:
We develop a rigorous mathematical framework to quantify defensive impact in basketball. Our core insight is that defensive effectiveness can be operationalized as a spatial regression problem, where a defender's position is modeled as a weighted sum of the ball, hoop, and opponent locations. This yields a hidden Markov model that estimates defensive matchups throughout each possession. From these matchups, we construct three sovereign primitives: counterpoint assignment, shot chart volume score, and shot chart disruption score. These operators are designed to satisfy anti-collinearity conditions by conditioning on offense-specific variables, ensuring that defensive metrics do not simply recapitulate offensive performance. Empirically, they provide a coherent picture of defensive value that complements traditional offensive statistics.
